blocks.instruction: Read each situation carefully and answer the questions.

items.label: (a)
items.q: Near the pond, Arya saw footprints in the mud. What could the students learn from these footprints? Name two animals that might have come to the pond to drink water.
items.answer: Footprints tell us which animals came to the pond, because different animals have different footprints (1). Any two: deer, tiger, rabbit, gaur (1).

answerPoints.point: Footprints show which animals visited; each animal's footprint is different
Any two animals: deer / tiger / rabbit / gaur

items.label: (b)
items.q: Sarthak saw a bird with a long tail and a large curved beak sitting on a tree. Name the bird and write how it got its name.
items.answer: Hornbill (1). It has a headgear growing out of its forehead like a horn, so it is called hornbill (1).

answerPoints.point: Headgear on the forehead like a horn gives it the name

items.label: (c)
items.q: A grasshopper hopped out of the grass. Arya said, 'This is an insect.' Write two features that show it is an insect.
items.answer: Any two (1 each): three pairs of legs; one pair of antennae to sense surroundings; sometimes two pairs of wings.

answerPoints.point: One pair of antennae / two pairs of wings (any one)

items.label: (d)
items.q: You are doing the food-picking activity with a spoon, a toothpick and a pair of sticks. Which tool would you use to pick grains, and which to pick a piece of fruit? What does this activity teach us about birds?
items.answer: Grains: spoon (or sticks); piece of fruit: toothpick/sticks — any sensible choice (1). It shows that birds have different beaks suited to the food they eat (1).

answerPoints.point: Sensible tool for each food item
Different beaks suit different foods; we can guess a bird's food from its beak

items.label: (e)
items.q: Mily collected a lemon leaf and a neem leaf. Write two ways in which the two leaves may be different from each other.
items.answer: Any two (1 each): colour, shape, size, texture (smooth/rough), smell, pattern of veins. Example: lemon leaf is oval and smooth with a strong smell; neem leaf is narrow with a toothed edge.

answerPoints.point: One difference (shape / size / colour / texture / smell / veins)

items.label: (a)
items.q: I am a big, red-coloured squirrel found in Pachmarhi and a few other places.

items.label: (b)
items.q: I look like a buffalo, but I am stronger and have shorter horns.

items.label: (c)
items.q: I am a type of crocodile with a long, narrow, pointed snout for catching fish.
Match the animal with its special feature.

pairs.right: Sharp curved beak and sharp claws
Long trunk to take food and water
Short strong beak to crack seeds

items.answer: Fish – fins to swim; Turtle – strong shell and webbed feet; Eagle – sharp curved beak and sharp claws; Elephant – long trunk to take food and water; Sparrow – short strong beak to crack seeds. 1 mark per correct pair.

items.q: The animal with a long trunk to take food and water.

items.q: The activity in which you rub a crayon over a paper placed on a leaf to get its shape.

blocks.instruction: Give two examples of each. (½ mark for each example)

items.label: (i)
items.q: Insects seen around your home
items.answer: Any two: ant, fly, mosquito, butterfly, bee, beetle, grasshopper, praying mantis (½ each).

items.label: (ii)
items.q: Animals that live in and around water
items.answer: Any two: fish, crab, frog, turtle, crocodile/gharial, water snake (½ each).

items.label: (iii)
items.q: Safety rules to follow in a forest
items.answer: Any two: do not tease animals; do not feed animals; do not damage trees and flowers; do not bring polythene bags; do not throw garbage; do not bring pets or weapons (½ each).

blocks.instruction: Sort the animals into the correct group: peacock, rabbit, crab, hornbill, deer, turtle, eagle, tiger. Write the group name against each pair.

items.label: (i)
items.q: Which two of these are birds in the sky?
items.answer: Any two of: peacock, hornbill, eagle (½ each).

items.label: (ii)
items.q: Which two of these are animals that live on land?
items.answer: Any two of: rabbit, deer, tiger (½ each).

items.label: (iii)
items.q: Which two of these live in and around water?

items.label: (iv)
items.q: Which of these animals in the list is a hunter with sharp claws that catches its prey from the sky?

blocks.instruction: Answer the following questions in two or three sentences.

items.label: (i)
items.q: Write three rules to be followed while visiting a zoo or a forest.
items.answer: Any three (1 each): be careful in a new place; do not tease animals; do not feed animals; do not damage trees and flowers; do not bring pets, firearms or weapons; do not bring polythene bags; do not damage public utilities; do not throw garbage.

items.label: (ii)
items.q: What special features do water animals have to help them survive? Give three examples.
items.answer: Fish have fins to swim (1); the gharial has a long, narrow, pointed snout to catch fish (1); turtles have strong shells for safety and webbed feet for swimming (1). Frogs can live both on land and in water — also acceptable.

answerPoints.point: Turtle – shell / webbed feet (or frog – land and water)

items.label: (iii)
items.q: How do leaves differ from one another? Mention three ways.
items.answer: Leaves differ in colour (1), shape and size (1), texture and the pattern of veins (1). Any three of colour, shape, size, texture, smell, vein pattern.

items.label: (iv)
items.q: How can we guess the eating habits of a bird? Explain with two examples.
items.answer: By observing its beak and claws (1). An eagle has a sharp, curved beak and sharp claws to catch prey (1). A sunbird has a long beak to drink nectar; a sparrow has a short, strong beak to crack seeds (1).

answerPoints.point: By looking at the beak and claws

items.label: (v)
items.q: What is an insect? Write its main features and name two insects.
items.answer: An insect is a tiny animal with three pairs of legs (1) and one pair of antennae; some have two pairs of wings (1). Examples: grasshopper, ant, bee, beetle, fly, butterfly, praying mantis (1 for two).

answerPoints.point: One pair of antennae / two pairs of wings

blocks.instruction: Complete the table in your answer book.

items.q: Copy and complete the table writing how each animal moves: Fish, Crab, Frog, Turtle, Snake.
items.answer: Fish – swims; Crab – walks (sideways); Frog – jumps/hops; Turtle – crawls (walks slowly) and swims; Snake – crawls/slithers. 1 mark each.

items.label: (i)
items.q: The state in which Pachmarhi is located.

items.label: (ii)
items.q: A colourful bird mentioned in the chapter.

items.label: (iii)
items.q: The vehicle in which the students went into the forest.

items.label: (iv)
items.q: The animal Sarthak saw munching on grass near the pond.

items.label: (i)
items.q: We should not throw garbage or bring polythene bags into a forest.
items.answer: Garbage and polythene harm the plants and animals — animals may eat plastic and fall ill, and it makes the forest dirty (1). The forest is the animals' home and we must keep it clean and safe (1).

answerPoints.point: Harms animals / plants, pollutes the forest
Forest is the animals' home; we must keep it safe

items.label: (ii)
items.q: Different plants and animals are dependent on each other.
items.answer: Plants give food and shelter to animals, e.g. a tree provides food to a bird (1). Animals help plants too, and if one part of the web of life disappears, the others are affected — like a tiger without deer (1).

answerPoints.point: Removing one living being affects others (web of life)

items.label: (iii)
items.q: An owl can hunt at night.
items.answer: Owls have very sharp eyesight (1) that helps them see clearly at night, so they can find their prey in the dark (1).

answerPoints.point: Helps it see and hunt in the dark

items.label: (i)
items.q: What is the role of a nature scientist?
items.answer: A nature scientist studies plants and animals (1) and helps others explore and understand nature, like Abha Didi guiding the students in the forest (1).

answerPoints.point: Guides / helps others explore and protect nature

items.label: (ii)
items.q: What happens in the 'Web of Life' game when one player is removed? What does it show?
items.answer: The web weakens or collapses (1). It shows that everything in nature is connected and depends on each other (1).

blocks.instruction: Answer in detail (five to six sentences).

items.label: (i)
items.q: Describe the nature trail at Pachmarhi. Who guided the students, what did they see near the forest entrance, and what did they see near the pond?
items.answer: The students went with their teacher to Pachmarhi in Madhya Pradesh (1). Abha Didi, a nature scientist, guided them (1). At the entrance they saw tall trees and chirping birds, then rode in jeeps and saw many plants and animals (1). Near the pond they saw gaur, footprints in the mud, a rabbit, and a hornbill on a tree (1). Presentation: complete sentences and correct order (1).

answerPoints.point: Guided by Abha Didi, a nature scientist
Tall trees, chirping birds, jeep ride

items.label: (ii)
items.q:
Which animal would you love to be? What special abilities would it give you? Write five sentences.
OR
Why is it important to protect the plants and animals in a forest? Write five sentences.
items.answer: First option: names an animal (1), describes at least two real abilities of that animal, e.g. eagle – sharp eyes and claws, fish – fins to swim (2), explains what those abilities would let the child do (1), writing in complete sentences (1). OR option: forests are homes of plants and animals (1); plants and animals depend on each other in the web of life (1); harming one affects the others (1); we get many things from nature (1); complete sentences (1).
items.markingGuide: Award full marks for five sensible, correct sentences on either option. 3 for three good sentences with one or two mistakes. 1 for a single relevant sentence.

items.q: Draw an insect (for example, a grasshopper or an ant) and label its three pairs of legs, antennae and wings.
items.answer: Drawing shows a body with six legs (three pairs) (1), antennae labelled (1), wings labelled or three body parts clearly drawn (1).
items.markingGuide: Neat drawing with all three labels correct — 3; drawing with two labels — 2; drawing with one label or unlabelled — 1.

items.q: You are planning a nature walk in a nearby park for your family, and you will be the guide. Write three things you will do to prepare, and one rule you will ask everyone to follow.
items.answer: Preparation, any two (1 each): identify a few plants and animals in the park; study their features and interesting facts; carry a bird diary/notebook; plan the route. Rule (1): e.g. do not pluck flowers, do not feed or tease animals, do not litter.
